Hi Oliver — great to meet earlier. Quick recap + next steps from our discovery on caching and pricing so we're aligned before I send an updated proposal.

Summary of what I heard from your team:
- Expected initial volume: ~150k calls / month (app-level requests)
- Avg tokens per call: ~150 token prompt (prefix + user context) + ~100 token generation = ~250 tokens/call
- Initial monthly token volume (approx): 150k * 250 = ~37.5M tokens/month
- Target budget for prod pilot: $5k–$15k/month (flexible depending on econ)
- Key ask: illustrate how caching (prefix cache) impacts effective $/1M tokens and total monthly cost under different hit-rate scenarios

A couple of asks for confirmation so I can finalize the proposal:
1) Is the 250 tokens/call reasonable for the majority of requests? If you have a sample of 100 requests we can estimate a more accurate token distribution.
2) How much personalization is in the prefix? If most prefixes are identical templates (or only have a few slot substitutions) we typically see much higher prefix cache hit rates.

I'll put together a two-page cost sheet showing effective $/1M tokens at 0/25/50/75% prefix hit rates and actual monthly spend for your 37.5M baseline. If that looks good, I'll include it in the updated proposal (attached).

Next steps: please confirm the two asks above and I'll send the updated proposal by Wednesday.

Thanks,

Hi Oliver — thanks for the telemetry, that’s super helpful. Below is a concise model we use in pricing proposals (I’ll attach the same table in the PDF). I’ll also call out assumptions so you can validate.

Pricing assumptions (example):
- Baseline model list price (for the workload / quality you requested): $12.00 per 1M tokens (this is our reference unit price for the selected generation model configuration in Redwood Dedicated/Hosted)
- Billing is per token consumed by the model invocation. Prefix cache reduces the number of tokens sent to the model when a prefix hit occurs.

Workload assumptions (your numbers):
- Avg tokens/call without cache: 250 tokens
- Calls/month: 150,000 -> baseline tokens/month = 37.5M

Effective token math (per-call):
- Let P = prefix tokens (140) and G = generated tokens (95). Total T = P + G (235 in your telemetry).
- If prefix cache hit rate = h, then tokens billed per call ≈ G + (1 - h) * P.

Examples (effective billed tokens / call and effective $/1M tokens):
- h = 0%: billed tokens/call = 235 -> billed tokens/month = 37.5M -> cost = (37.5M / 1M) * $12.00 = $450.00 * ? Wait — clarifying units: $12.00 per 1M tokens => cost = 37.5 * $12 = $450. (Right.)
- h = 25%: billed tokens/call = 95 + 0.75*140 = 95 + 105 = 200 -> billed/month = 30M -> cost = 30 * $12 = $360
- h = 50%: billed tokens/call = 95 + 0.5*140 = 95 + 70 = 165 -> billed/month = 24.75M -> cost = 24.75 * $12 = $297
- h = 70%: billed tokens/call = 95 + 0.3*140 = 95 + 42 = 137 -> billed/month = 20.55M -> cost = 20.55 * $12 = $246.60
- h = 75%: billed tokens/call = 95 + 0.25*140 = 95 + 35 = 130 -> billed/month = 19.5M -> cost = 19.5 * $12 = $234

Translated to effective $/1M tokens (i.e., cost / (baseline tokens / 1M) to compare apples-to-apples):
- h = 0% -> effective $/1M = $12.00
- h = 25% -> effective $/1M = (30 / 37.5) * $12 = $9.60
- h = 50% -> effective $/1M = (24.75 / 37.5) * $12 = $7.92
- h = 70% -> effective $/1M = (20.55 / 37.5) * $12 = $6.58
- h = 75% -> effective $/1M = (19.5 / 37.5) * $12 = $6.24

Notes & assumptions:
- We used your measured P=140 and G=95. If your prompts are closer to 250 total tokens then we should re-run — the math scales linearly.
- The price $12/1M is a reference. For committed volumes we can propose tiered discounts (eg. 10–30% based on committed monthly volume / term). I’ll include a sample tier in the PDF.
- Prefix cache hit rate is modeled as exact-match on a canonicalized prefix (we canonicalize common slot values and whitespace). That typically increases hit rate vs raw string matching.

Recommended next steps:
1) Pilot to measure real-world prefix hit rate over 2 weeks (we can help instrument) — we’ll then lock a recommended target hit-rate for pricing.
2) If pilot looks good, we’ll present a 3-month pilot proposal at the effective rates above + a commitment discount.
3) Engineering sync (Marcus) to discuss prompt canonicalization and session affinity to improve hits.

I’ve attached the PDF with the same table + a sample tiered discount. Let me know if you want me to run the same scenarios using $10/1M or $15/1M as alternate baselines — happy to include that in the proposal.

Cheers,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Follow-up: caching assumptions & next steps (technical notes)

Adding a couple of technical clarifications on the prefix cache model so expectations are aligned: 

1) Exact-match vs canonicalized match: our prefix cache operates on tokenized KV cache keys. We can canonicalize input (strip punctuation, normalize timestamps, replace user ids with stable slots) before keying — that materially increases hit rates for template-driven prompts.

2) What gets cached: the KV cache stores the transformer key/value state for the prefix tokens. A hit means we skip recomputing the prefix and only run the forward pass for the tail tokens. Practically this means large savings when P >> G, or when P is stable across requests.

3) Personalization: if prefixes include many per-user values (names, emails) hit rates drop. We recommend:
   - Move highly variable elements to the tail if possible
   - Use slot placeholders in the prefix and pass variable content as structured inputs we canonicalize server-side

4) Measurement: we can instrument sample traffic and return an estimated hit-rate distribution (per-template hit probability). The pilot will give you the ground-truth numbers we need for a binding pricing commitment.

Happy to do a 30-min sync this week to sketch canonicalization rules for your top 20 templates.

—Marcus
Director, Serving & Inference | Redwood Inference
